title.es: Una lista de permitidos que aguanta

tests:
allow = {"corp.example", "docs.python.org"}
assert is_allowed("https://corp.example/report", allow), "an exact host on the list is allowed"
assert is_allowed("https://wiki.corp.example/page", allow), "subdomains of an allowed host are allowed"
assert not is_allowed("https://corp.example.attacker.net/x", allow), "the substring trap: this host belongs to attacker.net"
assert not is_allowed("https://evilcorp.example/x", allow), "a host that merely ends with the same letters is not a subdomain"
assert not is_allowed("http://corp.example/x", allow), "only https is allowed"
assert not is_allowed("https://attacker.net/?q=corp.example", allow), "an allowed name in the query string does not count"
assert not is_allowed("https://corp.example@attacker.net/", allow), "the part before @ is user info, not the host"
assert is_allowed("https://CORP.example:443/x", allow), "hosts are case-insensitive and the port is not part of the host"
assert not is_allowed("javascript:alert(1)", allow), "non-http schemes are rejected"

hint.en: Parse once with `urlsplit`. Check `parts.scheme == "https"` and that `parts.hostname` is not `None`, then test `host == h or host.endswith("." + h)` for each allowed host.
hint.es: Analiza una vez con `urlsplit`. Comprueba `parts.scheme == "https"` y que `parts.hostname` no sea `None`, y después prueba `host == h or host.endswith("." + h)` para cada host permitido.

tests:
allow = {"docs.example"}
md = "See ![chart](https://docs.example/c.png) and ![x](https://attacker.net/p.png?d=SECRET)."
assert neutralize(md, allow) == "See ![chart](https://docs.example/c.png) and [image removed].", "the attacker image goes, the allowed image stays"
assert neutralize("[docs](https://docs.example/a) or [click](https://attacker.net/?d=1)", allow) == "[docs](https://docs.example/a) or click", "links to other hosts keep their text but lose the URL"
assert neutralize("no links here", allow) == "no links here", "plain text is unchanged"
assert neutralize("![a](http://docs.example/x.png)", allow) == "[image removed]", "an http URL is not allowed, even to a known host"
assert "attacker" not in neutralize("![](https://attacker.net/x) [](https://attacker.net/y)", allow), "empty alt or link text must not leave the URL behind"

hint.en: One regular expression can match both forms: `(!?)\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)\s]+)\)`. Use `re.sub` with a function that looks at the `!` group and checks the URL.
hint.es: Una sola expresión regular puede reconocer ambas formas: `(!?)\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)\s]+)\)`. Usa `re.sub` con una función que mire el grupo `!` y compruebe la URL.
